Describe rater centrality using RSM residuals and rater-specific PCM steps

Source: R/api-rater-centrality.R
rater_centrality_table.Rd

Place indirect centrality indices alongside their model basis, exposure and availability. These statistics describe fitted ratings; they do not classify raters or estimate a centrality parameter.

Usage

rater_centrality_table(fit = NULL, threshold_fit = NULL, rater_facet = "Rater")

Arguments

fit

Optional native additive RSM fit from fit_mfrm(), for residual versus expected-score correlations and ordinary Infit/Outfit.

threshold_fit

Optional native additive PCM fit with step_facet equal to rater_facet, for the spread of rater-specific step estimates. At least one of fit and threshold_fit must be supplied.

rater_facet

Name of the fitted non-Person rater facet.

Value

A list containing table (one row per rater), thresholds (category-ordered PCM step estimates), categories (counts on the retained roster), sources (model settings, estimates and readiness), settings and notes. Each index has an availability reason; source readiness is separate from numerical availability. Save with base::saveRDS() and reopen with base::readRDS(); export the data frames with utils::write.csv(). Reopening the result does not recalculate indices. This plain list has no dedicated plot() or automatic aggregate-report section. For a custom figure, retain each index's reason and source-status columns; do not mix threshold SD, residual correlation and fit on one scale. Graph centrality from rater_halo_network_analysis() has a different meaning.

Details

Eckes and Jin (2021, pp. 68-70, 77, 83-85) distinguish RSM residual-based indices from threshold SD under a rater-specific PCM. Accordingly, this function never assigns a shared RSM threshold SD to individual raters or substitutes a criterion-specific PCM for a rater-specific PCM. Supplying only one model leaves the other indices unavailable with an explicit reason. Both models must use the same retained response roster, including row multiplicities, category mapping, facet signs, centering and anchors. Row order may differ. Each model's estimator and readiness are retained.

Current support is ordinary JML or MML, unit observation weights, additive RSM/PCM and no facet shrinkage. Imported fits, interactions, generalized slope models, corrected JML, testlet and shared-random-rater models require their own definitions. There is no model fitting, quadrature or covariance estimation here. RSM response expectations are evaluated at saved point estimates using the same probability calculation as diagnose_mfrm(). MML uses saved Person EAP scores: these are plug-in expectations, not posterior-integrated or posterior-predictive expectations. Estimation and assignment effects can affect these indices even without true centrality.

ResidualExpectedCorrelation is the unweighted Pearson correlation of raw residuals (observed minus expected score) with expected scores within a rater. More negative correlations are consistent with scores compressed toward the middle. Standardized residuals are not used. A correlation requires at least two complete rows with nonconstant residuals and expected scores. Missing or nonfinite expectations, or a nonfinite primary Person/facet estimate involved in a row, make that rater's residual indices unavailable; incomplete subsets are not silently analyzed. Infit and Outfit additionally require strictly positive finite response variances in every row. Infit is sum(residual^2) / sum(variance); Outfit is mean(residual^2 / variance).

ThresholdSD is the sample SD across the complete set of a rater's m adjacent-category step estimates (divisor m - 1, explicitly chosen here; the paper does not specify the divisor). ThresholdVariance is its square. Larger spreads are consistent with centrality and smaller spreads with extremity. Steps are centered offsets in logits, not cumulative thresholds; adding the same rater severity/location to each step leaves their SD unchanged. At least two finite steps are required: a binary rubric cannot supply this spread. Steps are kept in category order. Disorder is reported, not repaired by sorting estimates; spread alone does not establish proper category functioning. ObservedSD describes the fitted internal score coding, with original-category labels retained in categories.

Infit/Outfit are supporting fit descriptions. Low Infit can also reflect halo, restricted score ranges or other mechanisms. No default .75, -.30 or 1.40 cutoff, combined flag, significance test or confidence interval is supplied. Threshold uncertainty, sparse exposure, different ability mixes, criterion mixtures and dependence between ratings affect interpretation. This function does not implement the Bayesian FM-SC centrality parameter omega, its uncertainty or ability adjustments, and does not reproduce FACETS numerical output merely by using related formulas. The package's ej2021 example data are synthetic, not the original TestDaF samples.

In the direct FM-SC model, rater severity shifts category locations while a positive rater-specific omega multiplies category step offsets. Omega therefore changes the response model and its ability estimates; it is not the SD of separately fitted PCM steps or a GPCM discrimination coefficient. Jin and Wang (2018) introduce this model; Eckes and Jin (2021, p. 71) give its RSM formulation. They are references for the distinction, not additional estimation methods available through this function.

References

Eckes, T., & Jin, K.-Y. (2021). Measuring rater centrality effects in writing assessment: A Bayesian facets modeling approach. Psychological Test and Assessment Modeling, 63(1), 65-94. Definitions and actual analyses: pp. 68-70 and 77; comparisons and limitations: pp. 83-88. Full text.

Jin, K.-Y., & Wang, W.-C. (2018). A new facets model for rater's centrality/extremity response style. Journal of Educational Measurement, 55(4), 543-563. doi:10.1111/jedm.12191 . Direct model, not implemented here.

See also

score_comparison_table(), interrater_agreement_table(), diagnose_mfrm(), mfrm_report(), mfrmr_methods_reference

Examples

ratings <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
rsm <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                method = "JML", model = "RSM", maxit = 100)
pcm <- fit_mfrm(ratings, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score",
                method = "JML", model = "PCM", step_facet = "Rater",
                maxit = 100)
centrality <- rater_centrality_table(rsm, pcm, rater_facet = "Rater")
centrality$table
